claim: RNA-mediated transcriptional gene silencing is a conserved process where small RNAs target transposons and other sequences for repression by establishing chromatin modifications.
source: RNA-mediated transcriptional gene silencing is a conserved process where small RNAs target transposons and other sequences for repression by establishing chromatin modifications.
evidence: This is a statement about established scientific knowledge in the field of RNA-mediated gene silencing.

claim: In Arabidopsis thaliana, long non-coding RNAs are produced by a specialized RNA polymerase known as Pol V.
source: A central element of this process are long non-coding RNAs (lncRNA), which in Arabidopsis thaliana are produced by a specialized RNA polymerase known as Pol V.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to established literature in the field.

claim: Non-coding transcription by Pol V is controlled by preexisting chromatin modifications located within the transcribed regions.
source: Here we show that non-coding transcription by Pol V is controlled by preexisting chromatin modifications located within the transcribed regions.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Most Pol V transcripts are associated with AGO4.
source: Most Pol V transcripts are associated with AGO4 but are not sliced by AGO4.
evidence: This claim is supported by RIP-seq experimental data showing AGO4 association with Pol V transcripts.

claim: Pol V transcripts are not sliced by AGO4.
source: Most Pol V transcripts are associated with AGO4 but are not sliced by AGO4.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing no evidence of AGO4 slicing activity on Pol V transcripts.

claim: Pol V-dependent DNA methylation is established on both strands of DNA.
source: Pol V-dependent DNA methylation is established on both strands of DNA and is tightly restricted to Pol V-transcribed regions.
evidence: This is supported by DNA methylation analysis data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Pol V-dependent DNA methylation is tightly restricted to Pol V-transcribed regions.
source: Pol V-dependent DNA methylation is established on both strands of DNA and is tightly restricted to Pol V-transcribed regions.
evidence: This is supported by comparative analysis of Pol V transcription and DNA methylation patterns.

claim: Chromatin modifications are established in close proximity to Pol V.
source: This indicates that chromatin modifications are established in close proximity to Pol V.
evidence: This is inferred from the tight spatial restriction of DNA methylation to Pol V-transcribed regions.

claim: Pol V transcription is preferentially enriched on edges of silenced transposable elements.
source: Finally, Pol V transcription is preferentially enriched on edges of silenced transposable elements, where Pol V transcribes into TEs.
evidence: This is supported by analysis of Pol V RIP-seq data on transposable elements.

claim: Pol V transcribes into transposable elements.
source: Finally, Pol V transcription is preferentially enriched on edges of silenced transposable elements, where Pol V transcribes into TEs.
evidence: This is supported by strand-specific analysis of Pol V transcription at TE boundaries.

claim: Pol V may play an important role in the determination of heterochromatin boundaries.
source: We propose that Pol V may play an important role in the determination of heterochromatin boundaries.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the observed enrichment of Pol V transcription at TE edges.

claim: RNA-directed DNA methylation (RdDM) takes place in most eukaryotic organisms and results in heterochromatin formation by the deposition of DNA methylation and repressive histone modifications.
source: RNA-mediated transcriptional gene silencing, in plants known as RNA-directed DNA methylation (RdDM), takes place in most eukaryotic organisms and results in heterochromatin formation by the deposition of DNA methylation and repressive histone modifications (Holoch and Moazed, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: RdDM relies on small RNAs, which usually are generated by the activities of an RNA-dependent RNA polymerase and Dicer.
source: This process relies on small RNAs, which usually are generated by the activities of an RNA-dependent RNA polymerase and Dicer.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field of RNA-mediated gene silencing.

claim: Small RNAs are incorporated into Argonaute and direct repressive chromatin modifications to complementary genomic regions.
source: Small RNAs are subsequently incorporated into Argonaute and direct repressive chromatin modifications to complementary genomic regions (Holoch and Moazed, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Recognition of target sequences by small RNAs requires ongoing non-coding transcription of the targets.
source: Recognition of target sequences by small RNAs requires ongoing non-coding transcription of the targets.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: Long non-coding RNA has been proposed to serve as a scaffold for Argonaute binding to chromatin, where incorporated small RNAs base pair with lncRNA.
source: This non-coding transcription gives rise to long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) which has been proposed to serve as a scaffold for Argonaute binding to chromatin, where incorporated small RNAs base pair with lncRNA (Holoch and Moazed, 2015).
evidence: This is a proposed model from the literature.

claim: Activity of Pol V is required for DNA methylation but not for the biosynthesis of the vast majority of small interfering RNAs (siRNAs).
source: Activity of Pol V is required for DNA methylation but not for the biosynthesis of the vast majority of small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) (Kanno et al., 2005; Lahmy et al., 2009; Pontier et al., 2005; Wierzbicki et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Pol V transcripts are believed to be capped or triphosphorylated on their 5' ends and not polyadenylated on their 3' ends.
source: Pol V transcripts are believed to be capped or triphosphorylated on their 5' ends and not polyadenylated on their 3' ends (Wierzbicki et al., 2008).
evidence: This is based on published literature.

claim: Pol V transcripts associate with several RNA binding proteins, including ARGONAUTE 4 (AGO4).
source: They associate with several RNA binding proteins, including ARGONAUTE 4 (AGO4) (Wierzbicki et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published work.

claim: siRNAs incorporated into AGO4 base pair with Pol V transcripts and recruit AGO4 to specific loci in the genome.
source: It has been proposed that siRNAs incorporated into AGO4 base pair with Pol V transcripts and recruit AGO4 to specific loci in the genome.
evidence: This is a proposed model in the field.

claim: Binding of AGO4 is followed by the binding of INVOLVED IN DE NOVO 2 (IDN2) which interacts with a subunit of the SWI/SNF ATP-dependent chromatin remodeling complex.
source: Binding of AGO4 is followed by the binding of INVOLVED IN DE NOVO 2 (IDN2) which interacts with a subunit of the SWI/SNF ATP-dependent chromatin remodeling complex (Böhmdorfer et al., 2014; Zhu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Pol V transcripts, AGO4, and/or other associated factors recruit DOMAINS REARRANGED METHYLTRANSFERASE 2 (DRM2), which is a de novo DNA methyltransferase.
source: Finally, Pol V transcripts, AGO4, and/or other associated factors recruit DOMAINS REARRANGED METHYLTRANSFERASE 2 (DRM2), which is a de novo DNA methyltransferase (Böhmdorfer et al., 2014; Gao et al., 2010; Zhong et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: DNA methylation is responsible for repression of Pol II transcription on silenced loci.
source: DNA methylation is then responsible for repression of Pol II transcription on silenced loci (Lister et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: siRNA biogenesis starts with the activity of Pol IV.
source: While Pol V is involved in the late stages of the RdDM pathway, siRNA biogenesis starts with the activity of another specialized RNA polymerase, Pol IV (Herr et al., 2005; Onodera et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Pol IV transcripts are substrates for RNA-DEPENDENT RNA POLYMERASE 2 (RDR2) and DICER-LIKE 3 (DCL3), which produce 24nt siRNAs.
source: Pol IV transcripts are substrates for RNA-DEPENDENT RNA POLYMERASE 2 (RDR2) and DICER-LIKE 3 (DCL3), which produce 24nt siRNAs (Haag et al., 2012; Li et al., 2015b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Pol V transcripts accumulate at low levels.
source: Unlike Pol IV transcripts, which are relatively abundant and have been characterized genome-wide (Blevins et al., 2015; Li et al., 2015b; Zhai et al., 2015), Pol V transcripts accumulate at low levels.
evidence: This is a known characteristic of Pol V transcripts that makes them difficult to study.

claim: Low accumulation of Pol V transcripts makes them difficult to detect using high-throughput sequencing approaches like RNA-seq.
source: This makes them difficult to detect using high-through sequencing approaches like RNA-seq.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the low abundance of Pol V transcripts.

claim: 4502 individual high confidence Pol V-associated transcripts were identified.
source: We used the RIP-seq data to annotate Pol V-associated RNAs genome-wide and identified 4502 individual high confidence Pol V-associated transcripts.
evidence: This is a direct result from the experimental data analysis.

claim: High levels of Pol V-associated transcription were observed throughout the predicted transcripts in both replicates.
source: We observed high levels of Pol V-associated transcription throughout the predicted transcripts in both replicates and only trace amounts of Pol V-associated transcription outside the annotations (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by the RIP-seq data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Only trace amounts of Pol V-associated transcription were observed outside the annotations.
source: We observed high levels of Pol V-associated transcription throughout the predicted transcripts in both replicates and only trace amounts of Pol V-associated transcription outside the annotations (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by the RIP-seq data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Signal strengths measured as differences between RPM normalized read counts in Col-0 and nrpe1 were significantly correlated (Pearson correlation r = 0.719, p<2.2*10–16).
source: Signal strengths measured as differences between RPM normalized read counts in Col-0 and nrpe1 were significantly correlated (Pearson correlation r = 0.719, p<2.2*10–16), which further increases confidence in the quality of our transcript calling.
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of the reproducibility between biological replicates.

claim: 20 loci had a strong reduction of RNA accumulation in nrpe1 in RT-qPCR.
source: We tested several newly identified Pol V-associated transcripts using locus-specific RT-qPCR and identified 20 loci which were suitable for primer design and had a strong reduction of RNA accumulation in nrpe1 in RT-qPCR (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR experimental data.

claim: Pol V binds chromatin at regions where Pol V-associated transcripts were detected.
source: We compared our RIP-seq with previously published Pol V ChIP-seq obtained using the same antibody (Wierzbicki et al., 2012) and found that Pol V binds chromatin at regions where we detected Pol V-associated transcripts (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by comparison of RIP-seq and ChIP-seq data.

claim: Pol V transcription was enriched on many genomic regions bound by Pol V.
source: Pol V transcription was also enriched on many genomic regions bound by Pol V (Wierzbicki et al., 2012) (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of Pol V ChIP-seq peaks.

claim: Most regions producing Pol V-associated transcripts displayed Pol V binding to chromatin and Pol V-dependent CHH methylation.
source: Most regions producing Pol V-associated transcripts also displayed Pol V binding to chromatin and Pol V-dependent CHH methylation (Stroud et al., 2013) which is a hallmark of RdDM (Figure 1E–G).
evidence: This is supported by integrated analysis of multiple datasets.

claim: RIP-seq is a much more sensitive approach for detecting genomic regions transcribed by Pol V than ChIP-seq.
source: In contrast, regions giving rise to Pol V-associated transcripts, which do not overlap Pol V ChIP-seq peaks, still displayed reduction of DNA methylation in nrpe1 (Figure 1G), suggesting that RIP-seq is a much more sensitive approach for detecting genomic regions transcribed by Pol V.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that RIP-seq detects regions with functional RdDM that are not detected by ChIP-seq.

claim: Pol V-associated RNAs identified using RIP-seq are produced by Pol V transcribing a genomic DNA template.
source: Overall, this analysis indicates that Pol V-associated transcripts are produced from regions bound by Pol V. Together with published in vitro data (Haag et al., 2012), these results suggest that Pol V-associated RNAs identified using RIP-seq are produced by Pol V transcribing a genomic DNA template.
evidence: This is inferred from the combination of RIP-seq, ChIP-seq data, and published in vitro data.

claim: Pol V transcripts originated from pericentromeric regions and from euchromatic chromosome arms.
source: Consistent with previously published data (Zheng et al., 2013; Zhong et al., 2012), Pol V transcripts originated from pericentromeric regions and from euchromatic chromosome arms (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of the genomic distribution of Pol V transcripts and citations to published literature.

claim: Pol V transcripts were preferentially produced from intergenic regions, gene promoters, and all transposon families except long terminal repeat (LTR) transposons.
source: Pol V transcripts were preferentially produced from intergenic regions, gene promoters, and all transposon families except long terminal repeat (LTR) transposons (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by enrichment analysis of Pol V transcripts across different genomic features.

claim: DNA methylation in the CG context was increased throughout the genomic regions transcribed by Pol V but not outside of those regions.
source: DNA methylation in the CG context was increased throughout the genomic regions transcribed by Pol V but not outside of those regions (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of bisulfite sequencing data.

claim: The levels of CG methylation were not sufficient to predict the levels of Pol V transcription.
source: Even though most Pol V transcripts were enriched in MET1-dependent CG methylation, the levels of CG methylation were not sufficient to predict the levels of Pol V transcription (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis between CG methylation and Pol V transcription levels.

claim: CG methylation and Pol V transcription overlap.
source: This observation shows that CG methylation and Pol V transcription overlap and provides support for preexisting CG methylation being an important factor in guiding Pol V to specific loci.
evidence: This is supported by the spatial overlap analysis of CG methylation and Pol V transcription.

claim: CG methylation does not regulate the level of Pol V transcription.
source: However, it also indicates that CG methylation does not regulate the level of Pol V transcription and that CG methylation is not needed upstream of transcription initiation sites.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of correlation between CG methylation levels and Pol V transcription levels.

claim: CG methylation may be required within the transcribed regions.
source: However, it also indicates that CG methylation does not regulate the level of Pol V transcription and that CG methylation is not needed upstream of transcription initiation sites. Instead it may be required within the transcribed regions.
evidence: This is speculated based on the observation that CG methylation overlaps with transcribed regions but not upstream.

claim: H3K9me2 overlapped Pol V-transcribed regions in a way similar to CG methylation.
source: We also tested if Pol V transcription overlaps with various posttranslational histone modifications (Moissiard et al., 2012; Greenberg et al., 2013; Luo et al., 2013) and found that H3K9me2 overlapped Pol V-transcribed regions in a way similar to CG methylation, while H3K4me2 was depleted on Pol V-transcribed regions (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of histone modification ChIP-seq data.

claim: H3K4me2 was depleted on Pol V-transcribed regions.
source: We also tested if Pol V transcription overlaps with various posttranslational histone modifications (Moissiard et al., 2012; Greenberg et al., 2013; Luo et al., 2013) and found that H3K9me2 overlapped Pol V-transcribed regions in a way similar to CG methylation, while H3K4me2 was depleted on Pol V-transcribed regions (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of histone modification ChIP-seq data.

claim: Five loci showed a significant reduction in the accumulation of Pol V transcripts in the met1 mutant.
source: Five loci showed a significant reduction in the accumulation of Pol V transcripts in the met1 mutant, which is consistent with a requirement of MET1 for Pol V transcription and with previous reports (Johnson et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data in the met1 mutant.

claim: The suvh4/5/6 mutant had a reduced accumulation of Pol V transcripts at two loci.
source: The suvh4/5/6 mutant had a reduced accumulation of Pol V transcripts at two loci (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), which indicates that SUVH4, 5, and 6 (and H3K9me2 they presumably establish) may have a more subtle or locus-specific effect on Pol V transcription.
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data in the suvh4/5/6 mutant.

claim: Pol V transcripts were significantly depleted on body-methylated genes, identified by high levels of CG methylation and low levels of CHH methylation.
source: Pol V transcripts were significantly depleted on body-methylated genes, identified by high levels of CG methylation and low levels of CHH methylation (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by enrichment analysis of Pol V transcripts on different categories of genes.

claim: Pol V transcripts were enriched on genes having high levels of CHH methylation.
source: In contrast, Pol V transcripts were enriched on genes having high levels of CHH methylation (Figure 2C), which are likely caused by intronic transposons (Saze et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by enrichment analysis and citation to published literature.

claim: CG methylation is not sufficient for Pol V transcription.
source: This suggests that CG methylation is not sufficient for Pol V transcription and consequently, CG methylation is one of many factors involved in guiding Pol V to specific genomic loci.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that body-methylated genes lack Pol V transcription despite having CG methylation.

claim: Pol V transcribed bidirectionally on annotated Pol V transcripts.
source: We found that, indeed, Pol V transcribed bidirectionally on annotated Pol V transcripts (Figure 2F) and that transcription levels on both strands were somewhat correlated (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by strand-specific analysis of Pol V RIP-seq data.

claim: Transcription on both strands was shifted with annotated Pol V transcripts on the reverse strand starting ~51 bp before annotated transcripts on the forward strand end.
source: Furthermore, transcription on both strands was shifted with annotated Pol V transcripts on the reverse strand starting ~51 bp before annotated transcripts on the forward strand end (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of the positions of forward and reverse Pol V transcripts.

claim: Actual RNAs produced from annotated Pol V transcripts are shorter than the size of these annotations.
source: This indicates that actual RNAs produced from annotated Pol V transcripts are shorter than the size of these annotations.
evidence: This is inferred from paired-end sequencing fragment length analysis.

claim: The median length of annotated Pol V transcripts is 689 bp.
source: Considering that the median length of annotated Pol V transcripts is 689 nt (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), this indicates that annotated Pol V transcripts contain more than one transcription initiation and/or termination site.
evidence: This is a direct measurement from the data.

claim: Annotated Pol V transcripts contain more than one transcription initiation and/or termination site.
source: Considering that the median length of annotated Pol V transcripts is 689 nt (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), this indicates that annotated Pol V transcripts contain more than one transcription initiation and/or termination site.
evidence: This is inferred from the discrepancy between annotated transcript length and actual RNA fragment length.

claim: Pol V is controlled by internal promoters.
source: Overall, our analysis suggests that Pol V is controlled by internal promoters, similar to what has been reported for a subset of Pol III transcripts (Geiduschek and Tocchini-Valentini, 1988).
evidence: This is inferred from multiple lines of evidence including bidirectional transcription and the presence of multiple initiation sites.

claim: Repressive chromatin modifications are at least important for Pol V recruitment.
source: Although any involvement of DNA sequence elements cannot be excluded at this time, our data are consistent with repressive chromatin modifications being at least important for Pol V recruitment and possibly working as a functional equivalent of a promoter.
evidence: This is inferred from the overlap of Pol V transcription with repressive chromatin marks.

claim: Pol V is required for AGO4 binding to chromatin genome-wide.
source: Pol V is required for AGO4 binding to chromatin genome-wide (Zheng et al., 2013), however, it is unknown if AGO4 associates with Pol V transcripts beyond the handful of loci tested so far (Wierzbicki et al., 2009; Böhmdorfer et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: AGO4 RIP-seq signal was significantly enriched on Pol V transcripts.
source: AGO4 RIP-seq signal was significantly enriched on Pol V transcripts (Figure 3A,B) and this binding was dependent on Pol V (Figures 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by AGO4 RIP-seq experimental data.

claim: AGO4 binding to Pol V transcripts was dependent on Pol V.
source: AGO4 RIP-seq signal was significantly enriched on Pol V transcripts (Figure 3A,B) and this binding was dependent on Pol V (Figures 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by comparison of AGO4 RIP-seq in wild-type and nrpe1 mutant.

claim: AGO4 associates with most if not all Pol V transcripts.
source: The presence of AGO4 RIP-seq signal on most transcripts shown on the heatmap (Figure 3A) indicates that AGO4 associates with most if not all Pol V transcripts.
evidence: This is inferred from the widespread AGO4 RIP-seq signal across Pol V transcripts.

claim: There is a significant correlation between Pol V and AGO4 RIP-seq signals.
source: This is further supported by a significant correlation between Pol V and AGO4 RIP-seq signals (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis of the two datasets.

claim: Association of AGO4 with RNAs produced by a polymerase other than Pol V does not lead to RdDM.
source: Regions generating those RNAs were not only not transcribed by Pol V but also failed to show any of the hallmarks of RdDM i.e. CHH methylation (Stroud et al., 2013), presence of siRNAs (Lee et al., 2012) or AGO4 binding to chromatin (Zheng et al., 2013) (Figure 3D). This suggests that association of AGO4 with RNAs produced by a polymerase other than Pol V does not lead to RdDM.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of RdDM hallmarks at Pol V-independent AGO4-bound transcripts.

claim: AGO4 associates with most Pol V transcripts and may have an additional role not related to RdDM.
source: We conclude that AGO4 associates with most Pol V transcripts and may have an additional role not related to RdDM.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of Pol V-independent AGO4 binding that does not lead to RdDM.

claim: Accumulation of Pol V transcripts was decreased in the ago4 mutant compared to Col-0.
source: We observed none of those effects (Figure 4A,B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1). In contrast, accumulation of Pol V transcripts was decreased in the ago4 mutant compared to Col-0 (Figure 4A,B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by Pol V RIP-seq data in the ago4 mutant.

claim: AGO4 does not slice Pol V transcripts.
source: These results indicate that AGO4 does not slice Pol V transcripts.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of evidence for slicing products and the reduction rather than increase of Pol V transcripts in ago4.

claim: AGO4 enhances Pol V transcription or stabilizes Pol V transcripts.
source: Instead, AGO4 seems to enhance Pol V transcription or to stabilize Pol V transcripts.
evidence: This is inferred from the reduction of Pol V transcript accumulation in ago4.

claim: Accumulation of Pol V transcripts was reduced in idn2.
source: We tested this possibility by performing RIP-seq with the anti-NRPE1 antibody in the idn2 mutant. Accumulation of Pol V transcripts was also reduced in idn2 (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1) over the entire lengths of the annotated transcripts (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by Pol V RIP-seq data in the idn2 mutant.

claim: IDN2 enhances Pol V transcription or increases the stability of Pol V transcripts on both strands.
source: This indicates that, like AGO4, IDN2 also enhances Pol V transcription or increases the stability of Pol V transcripts on both strands (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is inferred from the reduction of Pol V transcript accumulation in idn2.

claim: Effects observed in ago4 and idn2 were somewhat correlated.
source: Effects observed in ago4 and idn2 were somewhat correlated (Figure 4C) and could not be explained by an overall reduction of RNA levels in ago4 and idn2 as we did not observe a similar decrease on mRNAs (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis and comparison with mRNA levels.

claim: AGO4 and IDN2 are unlikely to contribute to slicing or other forms of degradation of Pol V transcripts.
source: Overall, our results show that AGO4 and IDN2 are unlikely to contribute to slicing or other forms of degradation of Pol V transcripts.
evidence: This is inferred from the reduction rather than increase of Pol V transcripts in ago4 and idn2 mutants.

claim: CHH methylation was significantly enriched within Pol V-transcribed sequences.
source: CHH methylation was significantly enriched within these sequences (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of CHH methylation data on Pol V transcripts.

claim: Only trace levels of CHH methylation were observed outside Pol V-transcribed regions.
source: However, only trace levels of CHH methylation were observed outside (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of CHH methylation data flanking Pol V transcripts.

claim: The RdDM pathway is only able to deposit DNA methylation within regions transcribed by Pol V.
source: This result shows that at least in genomic regions in close proximity to the annotated Pol V transcripts, the RdDM pathway is only able to deposit DNA methylation within regions transcribed by Pol V.
evidence: This is inferred from the tight spatial restriction of CHH methylation to Pol V-transcribed regions.

claim: Pol IV- and Pol V-dependent 24nt siRNAs mostly accumulated within regions transcribed by Pol V.
source: Analysis of previously published small RNA datasets (Lee et al., 2012) indicated that Pol IV- and Pol V-dependent 24nt siRNAs mostly accumulated within regions transcribed by Pol V (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1), indicating that Pol IV and Pol V likely transcribe the same genomic regions.
evidence: This is supported by analysis of small RNA data on Pol V transcripts.

claim: Pol IV and Pol V likely transcribe the same genomic regions.
source: Analysis of previously published small RNA datasets (Lee et al., 2012) indicated that Pol IV- and Pol V-dependent 24nt siRNAs mostly accumulated within regions transcribed by Pol V (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1), indicating that Pol IV and Pol V likely transcribe the same genomic regions.
evidence: This is inferred from the overlap of Pol IV- and Pol V-dependent siRNAs with Pol V transcripts.

claim: AGO4 associated with chromatin mostly within Pol V transcribed regions.
source: Similarly, AGO4 associated with chromatin (Zheng et al., 2013) mostly within Pol V transcribed regions (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of AGO4 ChIP-seq data on Pol V transcripts.

claim: Several features of RdDM are predominantly restricted between the start and the end of Pol V transcription.
source: These results show that, at least in genomic regions in close proximity to the annotated Pol V transcripts, several features of RdDM are predominantly restricted between the start and the end of Pol V transcription.
evidence: This is inferred from the spatial restriction of CHH methylation, siRNAs, and AGO4 binding to Pol V-transcribed regions.

claim: Pol V transcripts work in cis and mediate repressive chromatin modifications exclusively within transcribed regions.
source: Overall, these results are consistent with Pol V transcripts working in cis and mediating repressive chromatin modifications exclusively within transcribed regions.
evidence: This is inferred from the tight spatial restriction of RdDM features to Pol V-transcribed regions.

claim: There is no strand preference of DNA methylation relative to siRNAs or Pol V transcripts.
source: This indicates that there is no strand preference of DNA methylation relative to siRNAs or Pol V transcripts, which indicates that Pol V transcripts mediate the establishment of CHH methylation on both strands of DNA.
evidence: This is supported by strand-specific analysis of CHH methylation, siRNAs, and Pol V transcripts.

claim: Pol V transcripts mediate the establishment of CHH methylation on both strands of DNA.
source: This indicates that there is no strand preference of DNA methylation relative to siRNAs or Pol V transcripts, which indicates that Pol V transcripts mediate the establishment of CHH methylation on both strands of DNA.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of strand bias in CHH methylation.

claim: CHH methylation more closely follows AGO4 binding to Pol V transcripts than to DNA.
source: Interestingly AGO4 binding to DNA observed by ChIP-seq (Zheng et al., 2013) was strongly enriched on chromatin flanking these heterochromatic domains (Figure 6G). This indicates that CHH methylation more closely follows AGO4 binding to Pol V transcripts than to DNA, suggesting that AGO4 interaction with Pol V transcripts may be the primary event directing downstream factors of RdDM.
evidence: This is inferred from the spatial patterns of AGO4 RIP-seq, AGO4 ChIP-seq, and CHH methylation at heterochromatic domains.

claim: AGO4 interaction with Pol V transcripts may be the primary event directing downstream factors of RdDM.
source: This indicates that CHH methylation more closely follows AGO4 binding to Pol V transcripts than to DNA, suggesting that AGO4 interaction with Pol V transcripts may be the primary event directing downstream factors of RdDM.
evidence: This is speculated based on the closer spatial correspondence between AGO4 RIP and CHH methylation compared to AGO4 ChIP and CHH methylation.

claim: AGO4 binding outside of the heterochromatic regions was correlated with nucleosome density.
source: To test this possibility, we grouped heterochromatic domains by strength of H3 ChIP-seq signal (Moissiard et al., 2012), which should indicate nucleosome density. Indeed, AGO4 binding (Zheng et al., 2013) outside of the heterochromatic regions was correlated with nucleosome density (Figure 6H, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis between H3 ChIP-seq and AGO4 ChIP-seq signals.

claim: While short transposons were entirely transcribed by Pol V, longer TEs had a strong enrichment of Pol V transcription on their edges.
source: While short transposons were entirely transcribed by Pol V, longer TEs had a strong enrichment of Pol V transcription on their edges (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of Pol V RIP-seq data on transposons of different sizes.

claim: Euchromatic transposons longer than 4 kb displayed a strong enrichment of Pol V transcription and Pol V-dependent CHH methylation on their edges.
source: We further analyzed euchromatic transposons longer than 4 kb, similar to those studied by (Zemach et al., 2013). They also displayed a strong enrichment of Pol V transcription and Pol V-dependent CHH methylation (Stroud et al., 2013) on their edges (Figure 7B, Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of Pol V RIP-seq and CHH methylation data on large transposons.

claim: Regions inside the transposons appeared to be depleted in Pol V transcription compared to regions outside.
source: In contrast, regions inside the transposons appeared to be depleted in Pol V transcription compared to regions outside (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of Pol V RIP-seq data on large transposons.

claim: Pol IV transcripts were also enriched on edges of both categories of transposons, however, they were not depleted inside the transposons.
source: Pol IV transcripts (Blevins et al., 2015) were also enriched on edges of both categories of transposons, however, they were not depleted inside the transposons (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of Pol IV RNA-seq data on transposons.

claim: Transcription by both Pol IV and Pol V are involved in targeting RdDM to the edges of transposons.
source: These results indicate that transcription by both Pol IV and Pol V are involved in targeting RdDM to the edges of transposons.
evidence: This is inferred from the enrichment of both Pol IV and Pol V transcription at TE edges.

claim: Pol V transcription on the 5'-ends of transposons was enriched on the sense strand while Pol V transcription on the 3'-ends of transposons was enriched on the antisense strand.
source: Pol V transcription on the 5'-ends of transposons was enriched on the sense strand while Pol V transcription on the 3'-ends of transposons was enriched on the antisene strand. This indicates that Pol V transcripts showed an enrichment of Pol V transcription into the transposons at both ends (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is supported by strand-specific analysis of Pol V RIP-seq data at TE boundaries.

claim: Pol V preferentially transcribes into transposons.
source: These results indicate that Pol V preferentially transcribes into transposons.
evidence: This is inferred from the strand bias of Pol V transcription at TE boundaries.

claim: Pol V may play a key role in determining the boundaries of heterochromatin by transcribing into silenced regions.
source: Therefore, we propose that Pol V may play a key role in determining the boundaries of heterochromatin by transcribing into silenced regions.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the preferential transcription of Pol V into transposons at their edges.

claim: SUVH2 and SUVH9 are required for Pol V binding to chromatin and transcription.
source: Although de novo discovery of promoter elements is difficult even on Pol II genes (Molina and Grotewold, 2005) and requirement of short or variable sequence elements for Pol V transcription cannot be excluded, this is consistent with recent work showing the requirement of methyl-binding proteins SUVH2 and SUVH9 for Pol V binding to chromatin and transcription (Johnson et al., 2014; Liu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: SUVH2 and SUVH9 bind methylated DNA through their SRA domains.
source: Since SUVH2 and SUVH9 bind methylated DNA through their SRA domains (Johnson et al., 2008, 2014), this indicates that pre-existing DNA methylation may serve as an equivalent of the Pol V promoter.
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Pre-existing DNA methylation may serve as an equivalent of the Pol V promoter.
source: Since SUVH2 and SUVH9 bind methylated DNA through their SRA domains (Johnson et al., 2008, 2014), this indicates that pre-existing DNA methylation may serve as an equivalent of the Pol V promoter.
evidence: This is inferred from the requirement of SUVH2/9 for Pol V binding and their ability to bind methylated DNA.

claim: Pol V transcription is limited to the edges of transposons, while DNA methylation usually spans the entire lengths of the transposable elements.
source: Moreover, Pol V transcription is limited to the edges of transposons, while DNA methylation usually spans the entire lengths of the transposable elements.
evidence: This is supported by the data showing Pol V enrichment at TE edges.

claim: Pol V seems to behave more like Pol III in being controlled by features present within the transcribed regions.
source: Pol V seems to behave more like Pol III in being controlled by features present within the transcribed regions.
evidence: This is inferred from the evidence of internal control of Pol V transcription.

claim: RdDM of endogenous loci is mostly restricted to regions transcribed by Pol V.
source: First, our data demonstrate on a genome-wide scale that RdDM of endogenous loci is mostly restricted to regions transcribed by Pol V.
evidence: This is supported by the spatial restriction of RdDM features to Pol V-transcribed regions.

claim: Both strands of DNA are equally likely to be methylated even if siRNAs or Pol V transcripts show a strong strand preference.
source: Since we show that both strands of DNA are equally likely to be methylated even if siRNAs or Pol V transcripts show a strong strand preference, this could indicate that double stranded DNA is a substrate for DRM2.
evidence: This is supported by the lack of strand bias in CHH methylation.

claim: Double stranded DNA may be a substrate for DRM2.
source: Since we show that both strands of DNA are equally likely to be methylated even if siRNAs or Pol V transcripts show a strong strand preference, this could indicate that double stranded DNA is a substrate for DRM2.
evidence: This is speculated based on the lack of strand bias in methylation.

claim: The simplest explanation for the lack of strand bias in methylation would be base pairing between siRNAs and lncRNAs.
source: The simplest explanation for this observation would be base pairing between siRNAs and lncRNAs.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the data.

claim: The RdDM effector complex includes AGO4 throughout the genome.
source: Our data show that this effector complex includes AGO4 throughout the genome, however AGO4 does not slice Pol V transcripts.
evidence: This is supported by AGO4 RIP-seq data and the lack of evidence for slicing.

claim: IDN2 is involved in enhancing the accumulation of Pol V transcripts.
source: Previous work indicates the involvement of IDN2 (Böhmdorfer et al., 2014; Zhu et al., 2013), which also seems to be involved in enhancing the accumulation of Pol V transcripts.
evidence: This is supported by the reduction of Pol V transcripts in idn2 mutant.

claim: Base pairing between siRNAs and Pol V transcripts is likely to occur in close physical proximity to the Pol V complex.
source: If, as argued above, siRNAs incorporated into AGO4 base pair with Pol V transcripts, restriction of DNA methylation to Pol V-transcribed regions suggests that this base pairing is likely to occur in close physical proximity to the Pol V complex.
evidence: This is inferred from the tight spatial restriction of DNA methylation to Pol V-transcribed regions.

claim: AGO4 physically interacts with the C-terminal domain of Pol V.
source: This is consistent with observations that AGO4 physically interacts with the C-terminal domain of Pol V (El-Shami et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Transposons are stably silenced by the combined action of three silencing pathways.
source: Transposons are stably silenced by the combined action of three silencing pathways.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: Two silencing pathways are maintenance pathways which rely on CG methylation maintained by MET1 and non-CG methylation maintained by CMT2 and CMT3.
source: Two of them are maintenance pathways which rely on CG methylation maintained by MET1 (Lister et al., 2008) and non-CG methylation maintained by CMT2 and CMT3 (Stroud et al., 2014; Zemach et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: RdDM is capable of establishing DNA methylation de novo.
source: RdDM on the other hand is capable of establishing DNA methylation de novo.
evidence: This is established knowledge about RdDM.

claim: Mutations in RdDM components MOP1, MOP2, and MOP3 enhance spreading of euchromatin from genes into nearby transposons in maize.
source: The role of RdDM in the determination of heterochromatin boundaries has been recently studied in maize, where mutations in RdDM components MOP1, MOP2, and MOP3 enhance spreading of euchromatin from genes into nearby transposons (Li et al., 2015a).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published literature.
